rationale: C12 supplies the precise statutory and administrative framework that the child modifies: positions in General Schedule grades 16, 17, and 18 under section 710(a) of the Defense Production Act; agency requests submitted to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission; and Commission-controlled approval before employment. The child adds a numerical ceiling, suspends unfilled approvals, and requires review and recertification within that same machinery. C06 and C09 concern defense-emergency personnel administration through the Civil Service Commission, but they lack this distinctive supergrade-classification mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the number of positions in the Executive Branch which may be classified in grades GS-16, 17 and 18 under the authority contained in section 710(a) of the Defense Production Act of 1950, shall be 150
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The functions conferred upon the President by section 710(a) of the Defense Production Act of 1950 are hereby delegated as follows
shared_material.explanation: Both directives expressly operate under the same narrowly identified statutory authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: all agencies having responsibilities under the Defense Production Act have an equal opportunity to request the classification in grades GS-16, 17 and 18
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each officer or agency having functions under the said Act delegated or assigned to such officer or agency by this Executive order shall submit to the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission such requests for classification of positions in grades 16, 17, and 18 of the General Schedule
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C12's distinctive agency-request and Civil Service Commission classification process for the same three supergrades.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall not be filled until they are reviewed by the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission ... and recertified for classification to those grades by the Chairman
shared_material.parent_excerpt: No person shall be employed in a position of grade 16, 17, or 18 ... except pursuant to notice of the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission of the classification of the position.
shared_material.explanation: Both make action on a supergrade position contingent upon approval by the Commission chairman; the child adapts that control into review and recertification under a new aggregate limit.
